![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14268138/assets/26fe3edb60b89e021cb7fbb0660e92bc2d8199508e2c55180ff54fc34b87b084.png)

Which of the plots above represent irreflexive relations defined on the set $A=\{a,b,c\}?$
question.worked_solution:
A binary relation $R,$ defined on a set $A,$ is 

- *reflexive* if $(x,x)\in R$ for all $x\in A,$

- *irreflexive* if $(x,x)\notin R$ for all $x\in A.$

If some pairs of the form $(x,x)$ belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

Since $R$ must be irreflexive, we require 

$$
(a,a)\notin R,\,(b,b)\notin R,\,(c,c)\notin R.
$$

These ordered pairs correspond to the diagonal points on the plots, as shown below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14268138/assets/f8895e2787c1bf5a0191019f7583e414311d7df9d3dd08e2036d01173abd0579.png)

 

A plot corresponding to an irreflexive relation must not contain diagonal points. Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
